question: The Indo-Greek king who issued coins with bilingual inscriptions was:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Demetrius**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Demetrius I, also known as Demetrius Aniketos ("the Invincible"), was an Indo-Greek king who ruled in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• He is credited with issuing coins that featured **bilingual inscriptions** in Greek and Kharosthi, a script used in ancient India.
 
• The bilingual nature of his coins reflects his efforts to integrate Greek and Indian cultures and communicate with the diverse populations of his realm.
 
• Demetrius’ coins often depicted symbols such as the elephant, which was significant in Indian culture, symbolizing his connection to the region he ruled.
 
• He expanded his rule into northwestern India, marking the beginning of the Indo-Greek kingdom's influence in the subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Greek Kingdom:**

 
 
• The Indo-Greek kingdom was established in the regions of Bactria and northwestern India following the conquests of Alexander the Great.
 
• The blending of Greek and Indian cultures during this period is referred to as Greco-Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Bilingual Coinage:**
 
 
• Indo-Greek coins were unique for their use of both Greek and Indian scripts, typically Greek on the obverse and Kharosthi or Brahmi on the reverse.
 
• This bilingual approach was aimed at uniting the multicultural populations under their rule.
 
 
 
• **Kharosthi Script:**
 
 
• Kharosthi was an ancient script used primarily in Gandhara (modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan) and was derived from the Aramaic script.
 
• It was commonly used in inscriptions and coins during the Indo-Greek period.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism on Coins:**
 
 
• Indo-Greek coins often depicted symbols like elephants, lions, and the deity Zeus to appeal to both Greek and Indian traditions.
 
• These symbols also demonstrated the rulers' respect for local customs and beliefs.
 
 
 
• **Demetrius' Contribution:**
 
 
• Demetrius’ reign marked the beginning of Hellenistic influence in Indian art, culture, and governance, which persisted for centuries.
 
• He is considered a key figure in the history of cultural exchange between Greece and India.
